result.title: Joi-Bench-Task: Benchmarking Task Coordination in Full-duplex Voice Agents through Interactive Simulation
result.summary: Full-duplex voice agents enable natural, hands-free interaction, allowing users to refine requests, redirect ongoing work, and seek clarification while the agent is speaking. However, existing voice-agent benchmarks insufficiently isolate coordination between task execution and conversation. We introduce a benchmark that assesses this coordination by examining whether agents track what is being executed, what has been completed, what has been communicated, and what remains to be reported as the conversation evolves. We propose an interactive user simulator that introduces configurable interventions at designated timing in tool execution and spoken result delivery, supporting controllable and reproducible evaluation conditions. We evaluate five leading commercial voice agents along three dimensions: execution responsiveness, coordination under request changes, and coordination under interruptions. Agent evaluations reveal persistent coordination failures. Under request changes, the highest result completion rate is only 55%, indicating difficulty for current voice agents adapting to new requests while preserving earlier obligations. After user interruption, four of the five agents exhibit average information omission rates of at least 23%. These findings highlight task coordination as a central challenge for current voice agents in complex, evolving conversations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Joi-Bench-Task，用可在指定时机插入干预的交互式用户模拟器，评测全双工语音 agent 在任务执行与对话并行时追踪「正在做什么、已完成什么、已告知什么、还需汇报什么」的协调能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「请求变更与中断下任务状态是否保持、何时停止并完整汇报」的评测框架，可能为 LVR 关注的状态持续性与停止决策评价提供概念参照；但材料只涉及语音与工具执行协调，与视觉证据、内部 latent 表示无直接联系，迁移性需核查。
